items.title: Wayfair stock jumps more than 20% as retailer posts strongest U.S. growth since 2020
items.description: Wayfair, a pandemic darling that's seen sales slow since lockdown orders were lifted, posted its strongest U.S. growth since 2020 during its second quarter.

items.title: Palantir jumps 20% on 'otherworldly' commercial revenue — here's what's driving the demand
items.description: "Our customers have declined to become vassal states of the language labs," Palantir's co-founder and CEO Alex Karp said after blowout second-quarter earnings.

items.title: Foreigners are buying fewer U.S. properties, but luxury homebuilders still draw them in
items.description: Foreign buyers are pulling back sharply from U.S. residential real estate, in part due to a pullback among workers that would qualify for H-1B visas.

items.title: Polymarket in talks for fundraising round at more than $20 billion valuation
items.description: The reports come after the company told CNBC in June that its annualized revenue was well above $1 billion.

items.title: Pfizer tops estimates, hikes low end of revenue guidance on strength of Eliquis, other drugs
items.description: Pfizer said it cut its full-year revenue expectation for its Covid products to $4 billion, down from around $5 billion previously.

items.title: Philadelphia Fed President Paulson content with rates at current level, but keeping an open mind
items.description: Paulson said voting with the majority last week wasn't a tough decision.

items.title: Why Michigan voters are hearing 'communist' as they vote Tuesday
items.description: President Donald Trump and Republican allies are escalating attacks that label Democrats communists after progressive candidates won elections and primaries.

items.title: Analysis: How Bessent is pushing Warsh’s Fed to expand backstop for Japan’s yen defense
items.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants to defend the yen without selling Treasurys into a sensitive U.S. bond market. The Federal Reserve could help.

items.title: Jeff Bezos just filed to sell $4 billion in Amazon. The shares are falling
items.description: The filing came after Amazon climbed to an all-time high on Monday, extending gains sparked by last week's quarterly results.

items.title: Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market Tuesday
items.description: Stock futures are up as oil prices slide on hopes that a U.S.-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be near.

items.title: Bessent says there may be deal Tuesday or Wednesday to open Strait of Hormuz with 'freedom of movement'
items.description: "We are in talks with the Iranians," the Treasury secretary told CNBC's "Squawk Box."

items.title: Merck hikes revenue outlook as new drug sales grow, but cuts profit guidance due to deal charges
items.description: Merck cut its profit guidance due to a charge tied to its acquisition of biotech company Terns Pharmaceuticals.

items.title: ‘Last chance’: Bessent says Hormuz deal is in sight after Trump's warning on Iran talks
items.description: President Donald Trump has warned that the latest round of negotiations with Iran are the "last chance" to bring an end to the five-month conflict.

items.title: Bessent says U.S. backed Japan’s yen intervention to help stabilize Asia
items.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. bought yen alongside Japan to curb currency volatility and reduce risks to Asian markets.

items.title: Can your tax preparer use AI without telling you? Some experts say IRS rules aren't clear
items.description: A debate is brewing among tax practitioners regarding whether using AI to prepare tax returns should require a disclosure to clients.

items.title: Kalshi strikes partnership with compliance tech firm to help companies police insider trading
items.description: The company will announce a partnership with Comply, a compliance technology company, on Tuesday, Kalshi told CNBC.

items.title: McDonald's earnings beat estimates, chain announces new U.S. head to accelerate growth
items.description: McDonald's stock has fallen more than 11% this year, dragging its market cap down to roughly $191 billion.

items.title: McDonald's names company veteran Skye Anderson as its U.S. president as growth in its largest market slows
items.description: McDonald's new U.S. President Skye Anderson has been with the company for 26 years and succeeds Joe Erlinger in the role.

items.title: Apple launches fresh legal challenge against UK encrypted data access demand
items.description: The filing comes a year on from the U.K. dropping an initial demand for access to British and American user data from Apple.

items.title: Takaichi’s fiscal push could lift growth — and Japan’s already-rising interest bill
items.description: Japan is giving up revenue now in the hope that stronger consumption and a 370 trillion yen public-private investment will deliver faster growth later.
